newsitem.title: USA: EDS first quarter profits drop 11 percent.
newsitem.headline: EDS first quarter profits drop 11 percent.

text.p: Electronic Data Systems Corp reported a disappointing decline in first quarter profits Thursday and said it was taking a close look at its staffing levels.
But the computer services company also said it had strong new contracts and should catch up with Wall Street's expectations in the second half of 1997.
The Plano, Texas-based company said it had first quarter net income of $194.1 million, or 40 cents per share, down 11 percent from $218.8 million, or 45 cents per share, a year earlier.
The net earnings were about 20 percent short of analysts' expectations. EDS shares closed down $1 at $42 in consolidated New York Stock Exchange trading.
Operating revenues rose 6.7 percent -- slightly less than originally projected -- to $3.6 billion from $3.4 billion in the same period last year.
"We are not pleased with our earnings performance," EDS Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Les Alberthal said in a conference call. "It is certainly below what we wanted."

EDS executives said they had begun a comprehensive review and were looking at between 7,000 and 9,000 positions inside the company. It wants to save costs by moving some employees to new jobs and laying off others.
Vice Chairman Gary Fernandes said EDS would also take a second quarter charge related to a severance programme.

But the executives stressed that thousands more jobs were being created and it was not yet clear what the net effect would be on employment levels. About 98,000 people currently work for EDS worldwide.
Rapidly rising labour costs, especially for technical personnel, hurt EDS in the first quarter. Fernandes said labour and other costs would also have an impact on second quarter earnings.
"We expect the second quarter will be affected by many of the same conditions that affected us in the first quarter," Fernandes said.
But Alberthal said EDS would bounce back in the second half of the year and expects to meet analyst' expectations of 1997 earnings per share of between $2.30 and $2.35, excluding charges.

He said he was encouraged by $2.9 billion of new business signed in the three months ended March 31. "It was the third consecutive quarter of very strong new contract signings ... It demonstrates the strength of marketplace and our ability to be effective and successful."

Since winning its independence from General Motors Corp. in June, EDS has disappointed investors by showing only moderate revenue growth, but Fernandes said the situation would improve markedly in the second half of the year.
"We believe we are still able to deliver a very solid year ... that continues a very long record of double digit growth in earnings per share for EDS," Fernandes said.
